text: The ledger intake of rwb-source-data consumes the six event types of section 12.4: rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1, rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1, rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1 and rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1 on rwb.case.events.v1 (P3), rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 on rwb.document.events.v1 (P5) and rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 on rwb.decision-record.v1 (P7), read from the legacy listener's EV-01, EV-02, EV-04, EV-19, EV-16 and EV-08 and from rows 01, 02, 04, 19, 16 and 08 of the Architecture v5 event catalogue. The hit count of a repeated idempotency key is held by the PLT inbox table processed_event created in rwb_source_data, so this story adds no table and the legacy Flyway migration for processed_event is not part of the split.
why: The legacy story names its six inputs by the monolith's event numbers and creates its own processed_event table; the target catalogue gives a name and a topic for each fact but does not name rwb-source-data as a consumer, and the Ownership Map makes processed_event and idempotency_key PLT library objects created in each service's schema, so the intake set and the hit-count table have to be fixed by assumption before the listener can be built.

impact: The listener can be built and tested against the six fixtures from Day 1; if the catalogue later names a different consumer set or a different type name, the change is one map row and one fixture in RWB-P1-E1067-CON, not a rewrite of the consumer.

text: The ledger intake contract baseline is published as a versioned YAML map with one row per consumed event type and the row fields eventType, topic, owner, entryEventCode, sourceSystem, sourceRefForm, actorSource, payloadFields and acceptedVersions, with the version label as a field of the document; the document fact and the timer fact are read as rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 on rwb.document.events.v1 and rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1 on rwb.case.events.v1, the rows 16 and 19 of the Architecture v5 event catalogue, with EV-16 and EV-19 kept as row labels beside them.
why: No source gives the artefact, the file format or the version label of the intake contract, and no source states which target types carry the document and timer facts into the ledger; the legacy story gives only its own event numbers and a configuration key.
